title: API Rate Limits v3.2
content: The REST Orders endpoint allows 180 requests per minute per account. Market data REST endpoints allow 600 requests per minute per account. Limits are enforced on a rolling 60-second window. When a limit is exceeded the API returns HTTP 429 with the headers X-RateLimit-Remaining and Retry-After. Clients should wait for the Retry-After interval and then retry with exponential backoff and jitter. This version supersedes Rate Limits v2.1.

title: API Rate Limits v2.1
content: Version 2.1 allowed 120 requests per minute for the REST Orders endpoint and 300 requests per minute for market data endpoints. Limits were enforced on a fixed one-minute window that reset at the start of each minute. This policy was superseded by Rate Limits v3.2 on 1 October 2025.

title: API Error Handling Guide v3.2
content: HTTP 400 means the request body failed validation. HTTP 401 means the access token is missing, expired, or invalid. HTTP 403 means the token is valid but lacks the required scope or account permission. HTTP 409 means an idempotency key was reused with a different request body. HTTP 429 means the request was throttled by a rate limit and is not an authentication failure. HTTP 500 and 503 indicate a server-side problem; retry these with exponential backoff. Do not retry 400, 401, or 403 responses without fixing the request.

title: API Authentication v3.2
content: Server integrations authenticate with the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow. Exchange the client ID and client secret at the token endpoint for an access token. Send the access token in the Authorization header as a Bearer token. Access tokens expire after 60 minutes; request a new token before expiry rather than retrying after a 401. This version supersedes the static API key scheme in Authentication v2.1.

title: API Authentication v2.1
content: Version 2.1 authenticated requests with a static API key sent in the X-API-Key header. Static API keys did not expire. The static key scheme was deprecated in v3.2 and stopped being accepted on 31 December 2025.

title: Credential Management and Rotation
content: Rotate client secrets at least every 90 days. Each credential is issued with scopes such as orders:read, orders:write, and marketdata:read; request only the scopes an integration needs. Revoke a credential immediately in the developer console if it is exposed, then issue a replacement. Never embed client secrets in browser or mobile application code.

title: Pagination v3.2
content: List endpoints use cursor pagination. Pass the next_cursor value from the previous response to fetch the following page. The default page size is 50 and the maximum is 200 items. Do not rely on numeric offsets, because results can shift while orders are being created.

title: WebSocket Connection Behaviour v3.2
content: The WebSocket server sends a heartbeat every 30 seconds. A connection that misses two consecutive heartbeats is closed by the server. After an unexpected close, reconnect with exponential backoff and resubscribe to every channel, because subscriptions are not restored automatically. Each connection supports up to 50 channel subscriptions.

title: Idempotency Keys
content: Send an Idempotency-Key header when creating orders so that retries cannot create duplicate orders. A repeated request with the same key and body returns the original response. Keys are retained for 24 hours. Reusing a key with a different request body returns HTTP 409.

title: Client Timeout Recommendations
content: Configure a connect timeout of 10 seconds and a read timeout of 30 seconds for REST calls. If an order request times out, query the order by its idempotency key before resending, because the original order may have been accepted.

title: Webhook Notifications
content: Webhooks deliver order status events such as accepted, partially filled, filled, cancelled, and rejected. Each delivery is signed with HMAC-SHA256 and the signature is sent in the X-TradeFlow-Signature header. Verify the signature before processing the event. Failed deliveries are retried up to 5 times over 24 hours.

title: Sandbox Environment
content: The sandbox environment mirrors the production API with simulated fills and test funds. Sandbox accounts receive 100,000 in test funds. Sandbox data is reset every Sunday, so integrations should not depend on sandbox orders persisting.

title: Request IDs and Tracing
content: Every API response includes an X-Request-ID header. Log this value with your own request logs. Include the X-Request-ID and the UTC timestamp when contacting support so engineers can trace the request.

title: API Versioning and Deprecation Policy
content: TradeFlow gives at least six months notice before removing an API version or field. Deprecated endpoints return a Sunset header with the removal date. Breaking changes are announced in the release notes and by email to registered developers.

title: Market Data API
content: The market data API provides quote snapshots over REST and streaming quotes over WebSocket. Accounts without a real-time data subscription receive quotes delayed by 15 minutes. Real-time data requires an active market data subscription on the account.

title: Release Notes v3.2
content: Release 3.2 raised the Orders endpoint limit from 120 to 180 requests per minute and moved rate limiting to a rolling window. It made OAuth 2.0 client credentials mandatory for new integrations and introduced cursor pagination for list endpoints.

title: Order Types v1.4
content: TradeFlow supports market, limit, stop, and stop-limit orders. A market order executes at the best available price and does not guarantee the fill price; fast markets can cause slippage. A limit order executes only at the limit price or better. A stop order becomes a market order when the stop price is reached.

title: Order Rejection Troubleshooting v1.4
content: Every rejected order includes a rejection code that identifies the failed validation. Common codes are INSUFFICIENT_BUYING_POWER, MARKET_CLOSED, PRICE_BAND, PERMISSION_DENIED, and MIN_QUANTITY. Check instrument status, market hours, buying power, price bands, account permissions, and minimum order quantity.

title: Cancelling and Amending Orders
content: Open orders can be cancelled or amended until they are fully filled. Cancelling a partially filled order cancels only the remaining unfilled quantity. A cancellation request is not guaranteed to succeed if the order fills first; confirm the final status with the order status endpoint or webhook.

title: Market Hours v1.1
content: Trading availability follows the exchange schedule shown for each instrument. Orders submitted while the market is closed are rejected with MARKET_CLOSED unless they are queued as day orders for the next session. Exchange holidays and volatility halts can change availability.

title: Trading Permissions
content: Cash trading in equities is enabled for every verified account. Margin trading and options trading each require a separate application and approval. Orders for a product the account is not approved for are rejected with PERMISSION_DENIED.

title: Price Bands and Volatility Halts
content: Limit orders priced more than 10 percent away from the last traded price are rejected with the PRICE_BAND code. During an exchange volatility halt, new orders for the instrument are rejected until trading resumes.

title: Trade Settlement
content: Equity trades settle one business day after the trade date (T+1). Proceeds from a sale can be used to buy other securities immediately, but unsettled proceeds cannot be withdrawn until settlement completes.

title: Margin Requirements
content: Margin accounts must keep equity of at least 25 percent of the market value of margined positions. If equity falls below this maintenance requirement, TradeFlow issues a margin call that must be met within 3 business days. TradeFlow may liquidate positions without notice if the deficit is not covered.

title: Fee Schedule
content: Equity orders are charged 0.005 per share with a minimum of 1.00 per order. There is no fee for deposits or for API access. Real-time market data subscriptions are billed monthly. Outbound wire withdrawals are charged 15.00 each.

title: Corporate Actions
content: Stock splits adjust position quantity and cost basis automatically on the effective date. Cash dividends are credited to the account on the payment date. Open orders for an affected instrument may be cancelled before a split takes effect.

title: Pre-Trade Risk Controls
content: Each account has a default maximum order notional of 1,000,000 per order. Orders above the limit are rejected before reaching the exchange. Account owners can request a lower or higher limit through support.

title: Withdrawal Requirements v2.0
content: Withdrawals require a verified account, two-factor authentication, and a linked bank account in the account holder's name. A 48-hour security hold applies after a password reset or after a new bank account is linked. Approved withdrawals are processed within 1 to 3 business days. This version supersedes Withdrawal Requirements v1.3.

title: Withdrawal Requirements v1.3
content: Under version 1.3, two-factor authentication was optional for withdrawals and a 24-hour security hold applied after a password reset. This policy was replaced by Withdrawal Requirements v2.0 in July 2025.

title: Deposits
content: Accounts are funded by bank transfer from an account in the account holder's name. Card payments are not accepted. Deposits normally clear within 1 to 2 business days and appear as pending until they clear.

title: Identity Verification
content: To verify an account, upload a government-issued photo ID and a proof of address dated within the last three months. Reviews are usually completed within 2 business days. Unverified accounts cannot trade or withdraw funds.

title: Account Restrictions
content: An account can be restricted after failed identity verification, an unresolved margin call, or suspected unauthorised activity. A restricted account can close existing positions but cannot open new ones. Support explains the reason and the steps required to lift the restriction.

title: Closing an Account
content: To close an account, close or transfer all open positions and withdraw the remaining balance, then submit a closure request. Closure is completed within 30 days. Statements remain available after closure.

title: Two-Factor Authentication
content: Two-factor authentication can use an authenticator app or SMS codes; an authenticator app is recommended. When 2FA is enabled, ten single-use backup codes are issued. Store backup codes offline.

title: Account Recovery
content: If you lose your two-factor device and have no backup codes, request a 2FA reset from the login page. Resets require identity re-verification and take up to 3 business days. A 48-hour withdrawal hold applies after a reset.

title: Statements and Tax Documents
content: Monthly account statements are available in the documents section. Annual tax forms are published by 15 February for the previous year. TradeFlow does not provide tax advice; consult a qualified tax adviser.

title: Notification Settings
content: Order fill, deposit, and withdrawal notifications can be sent by email or push notification. Price alerts can be set on any instrument and trigger once when the price crosses the chosen level. Security notifications cannot be turned off.

title: Data Retention
content: Order and trade records are retained for seven years to meet regulatory requirements. Support chat transcripts are retained for two years. Records required by regulation cannot be deleted on request.

title: Suspicious Login Response v1.2
content: If you see an unfamiliar login, reset your password, revoke all active sessions, rotate any API credentials, and contact support. Never share one-time codes with anyone, including people claiming to be TradeFlow staff.

title: Phishing Awareness
content: TradeFlow will never ask for your password, one-time codes, or client secrets by email, phone, or chat. Official emails come only from the tradeflow.example domain. Forward suspicious messages to the security team and do not click their links.

title: Session Management
content: Web sessions expire after 12 hours of inactivity. Active sessions and devices are listed under security settings, where any session can be revoked. Changing the password revokes all other sessions.

title: API IP Allowlisting
content: Each API credential can be restricted to up to 10 IP address ranges in CIDR notation. Requests from addresses outside the allowlist are rejected with HTTP 403. Changes to the allowlist take effect within 5 minutes.

title: Incident 2025-04: Elevated Order API Latency
content: On 22 April 2025, p95 latency on the Orders API rose above 4 seconds for 47 minutes and some requests timed out. The root cause was database connection pool exhaustion after a configuration change. The pool capacity was increased and saturation alerts were added.

title: Incident 2025-09: REST API Throttling
content: On 8 September 2025, a traffic burst from a misconfigured client caused elevated HTTP 429 responses for 18 minutes. Rate limits were not changed. Customers were advised to honour Retry-After and use exponential backoff.

title: Incident 2025-06: WebSocket Disconnections
content: On 11 June 2025, WebSocket clients were disconnected every 60 seconds for about two hours. A load balancer idle timeout had been set below the heartbeat interval. The timeout was restored to 120 seconds and a configuration check was added.

title: Maintenance Windows
content: Scheduled maintenance takes place on Sundays between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. During maintenance the API may return HTTP 503 with a Retry-After header. Maintenance is announced on the status page at least 72 hours in advance.

title: Service Status and Degradation
content: Current service health is published on the TradeFlow status page, including degraded performance and outages. Subscribers receive email updates when an incident is opened, updated, and resolved. A postmortem is published within 5 business days of a major incident.

title: Support Escalation Process
content: Before escalating, collect the account ID, the X-Request-ID values, UTC timestamps, and the exact error response. Severity 1 issues, such as being unable to trade, receive a first response within 1 hour. Severity 2 issues receive a first response within 8 business hours.

title: Service Level Targets
content: TradeFlow targets 99.9 percent monthly availability for the REST API, excluding scheduled maintenance. Availability is measured from external probes every minute.

title: Client Monitoring Recommendations
content: Integrations should monitor their HTTP 429 rate, p95 request latency, WebSocket reconnect count, and order rejection codes. Alert when the 429 rate rises above 1 percent of requests, because it usually means retries are not honouring Retry-After.

title: Audit Log
content: The audit log records logins, credential changes, permission changes, and withdrawals. Audit events are retained for one year and can be exported as CSV from the security settings.

title: Official SDKs
content: TradeFlow publishes official SDKs for Python and JavaScript. Both SDKs refresh OAuth tokens automatically and retry HTTP 429 and 503 responses with exponential backoff that honours Retry-After.
